newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU to study Finnish criticism of EU feed additive rules.
newsitem.headline: EU to study Finnish criticism of EU feed additive rules.

text.p: The European Commission will examine as soon as possible a Finnish complaint about contradictory EU rules on the use of additives in animal feed, Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Tuesday.
Finnish Farm Minister Kalevi Hemila complained at the EU Farm Council that some antibiotics, such as Spyromicin and Tylosin, were allowed in animal feed but banned in veterinary medicine.
When it joined the EU in 1995, Finland was granted a derogation from EU rules and authorised to ban these products in animal feed until the end of 1997.
Finland recently submitted scientific evidence to support its demand to continue the ban beyond 1997.
It argues that prolonged use of the antibiotics as feed additives would build up bacteria resistance and reduce the effectiveness of the drugs in combatting animal diseases.
